stories.title: Nvidia is buying Hugging Face for almost $13 billion
stories.author: Jess Weatherbed
bullet_points: Nvidia is acquiring Hugging Face for approximately $12.93 billion.
The acquisition places the leading open-source AI platform under the control of the major AI chipmaker.
This move signals a major industry consolidation trend as hardware giants integrate with key AI software ecosystems.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
Indicates the model is relevant for text-generation tasks.
Categorizes the model under key AI/ML technologies like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Meta Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model released under the permissive Apache 2.0 license.
It is specifically designed for local coding agents and is optimized via Ollama's MLX engine with new DFlash and image input support.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights a trending model, DeepSeek-R1, on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
The model is categorized under text-generation and utilizes transformers and safetensors.
It is associated with the DeepSeek-V3 architecture and conversational AI applications.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of Meta-Llama-3-8B on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
It pertains to the text-generation pipeline, indicating its use in large language model applications.
The associated tags confirm its relevance within the transformers and llama ecosystem.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning is now accessible via Ollama.
It is a 30 billion parameter open model optimized for agentic workflows.
The model is designed for local hardware execution, supporting continuous context gathering and tool use for multi-step tasks.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 performance is significantly boosted in Ollama 0.31 when running on Apple Silicon.
The speed improvement is achieved through Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Performance gains reach up to 90% faster, particularly when utilized with coding agents as benchmarked by Aider.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon through updates to its MLX engine.
The performance improvements result in faster response times and higher quality model outputs.
The updated engine also demonstrates better memory efficiency when running models on Apple Silicon.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, providing an open-source framework for personal AI agents.
The framework emphasizes 'local-first' operation, allowing AI to run entirely on user hardware.
It features built-in support for Ollama, facilitating the use of local LLMs.

stories.title: Microsoft discloses Azure revenue as part of major financial reporting changes
stories.author: Tom Warren
bullet_points: Microsoft is restructuring its financial reporting by splitting its businesses into two segments.
The company is disclosing Azure cloud revenue quarterly for the first time.
These changes are intended to better reflect the operational impact of AI on Microsoft.

stories.title: FCC plans robocall scorecard to grade phone companies on spam call blocking
stories.author: Jon Brodkin
bullet_points: The FCC is planning to implement a scorecard system to evaluate phone carriers.
This scorecard will grade companies based on their effectiveness in blocking spam and robocalls.
Metrics for the scorecards will likely include call-blocking statistics and customer complaint data.

stories.title: US court rules Google will not have to sell ad exchange after losing antitrust case
stories.author: Ryan Whitwam
bullet_points: US court ruled against Google regarding its ad exchange practices after an antitrust case.
The Department of Justice (DOJ) successfully proved illegal conduct by Google.
However, the court decision did not mandate the divestiture (sale) of the ad exchange, limiting the DOJ's desired outcome.

stories.title: The Army just used a 20-kilowatt laser to take out three drones
stories.author: Fernanda González, wired.com
bullet_points: The U.S. Army has successfully deployed a 20-kilowatt laser system.
The system is capable of tracking and neutralizing hostile drones.
This represents a significant advancement in directed energy weapons for defense applications.

stories.title: Post-Training Language Models for Gold-Medal Performance in Coding Competitions
stories.author: Boris Ginsburg
bullet_points: The research focuses on specializing large language models (LLMs) for high-level performance in competitive programming (e.g., IOI, ICPC).
The proposed methodology is an end-to-end pipeline integrating large-scale problem curation, synthetic reasoning traces, Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT), and Reinforcement Learning (RL).
Two models, Nemotron-3-Nano-CC (30B) and Nemotron-3-Ultra-CC (550B), were trained using this pipeline, demonstrating the impact of different training regimes.

stories.title: Untangling the Mechanisms of Misleading Context in Medical Question Answering
stories.author: Noémie Elhadad
bullet_points: Investigates how misleading context can corrupt the expert-level medical judgment of Large Language Models (LLMs).
The research examines the model's susceptibility to context, the mechanism of corrupted reasoning, and decision monitorability.
Uses the MedMisBench dataset to analyze these vulnerabilities in medical question answering.

stories.title: Repo-To-Skill: Distilling GitHub Repositories Into AI4AI Skills
stories.author: Zheng Liu
bullet_points: The research addresses the gap between advanced AI agents and practical, domain-specific operational knowledge.
The core idea, 'Repo-To-Skill,' involves distilling complex knowledge embedded in GitHub repositories into usable AI skills.
This work aims to bridge the gap where current autonomous agents know methods but lack the practical 'know-how' to execute them effectively.

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a third-party gateway.
This integration allows users to run open-source models within the Claude Desktop environment.
It bridges proprietary AI platforms with local, open-source LLM ecosystems.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release brings enhanced performance and broader GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to expand model support across diverse hardware configurations.
It improves the capabilities of Ollama's MLX engine, particularly on Apple silicon.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA is introducing Nemotron 3 Ultra.
The model is specifically designed for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is optimized for supporting long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: TCL’s new Nxtpaper phone offers both e-reader and OLED
stories.author: Dominic Preston
bullet_points: TCL's new P80 Ultra phone integrates an E Ink-esque Nxtpaper display technology.
The phone offers the unique capability to switch between a standard display and a low-power, monochromatic 'paper' mode.
This iteration upgrades the previous LCD models by implementing the Nxtpaper feature on an OLED panel.

stories.title: I rented a car, and within hours, my driver's license was for sale
stories.author: Dan Goodin
bullet_points: A massive, real-time data breach is reportedly under FBI investigation.
The breach is severe enough to compromise personal data, exemplified by a driver's license being listed for sale.
The incident highlights significant risks associated with personal data security and digital identity theft.

stories.title: Wary of Artemis IV timeline, NASA is changing lunar spacesuit design
stories.author: Eric Berger
bullet_points: NASA is modifying the design of the lunar spacesuit.
The changes are being made in response to concerns regarding the Artemis IV timeline.
The adjustments reflect the specific needs of near-term lunar missions.

stories.title: Google releases Gemini 3.8 Flash, its third Flash model in six weeks
stories.author: Ryan Whitwam
bullet_points: Google has released Gemini 3.8 Flash, indicating continued rapid iteration in its AI model lineup.
The release follows a period where updates to the main Gemini Pro model appeared to have paused.
The frequent release of 'Flash' models suggests a focus on optimizing for speed and efficiency in Google's AI offerings.

stories.title: Trump may be forced to reveal secret rules feds use for AI safety testing
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: A lawsuit alleges that Trump's review process for frontier AI models involves secret rules.
The core concern raised is the potential for corruption within these undisclosed federal AI safety testing procedures.
The story touches upon the intersection of political oversight, AI safety regulation, and legal scrutiny.

stories.title: Is Russia's rival to Starlink failing? Here's what we know.
stories.author: Stephen Clark
bullet_points: The article discusses potential failures within Rassvet, a satellite constellation rivaling Starlink.
Initial data suggests at least three of the first 32 Rassvet satellites have experienced outright failures.
The report indicates that there may be additional satellites within the constellation that are also experiencing issues.

stories.title: Discriminative World Models for Web Agents
stories.author: Roei Herzig
bullet_points: Current web agents utilize world models for action selection by predicting future web states.
These models are often trained using supervised next-state prediction, yielding fixed state representations (e.g., HTML snapshots).
The training objective is noted as being misaligned with the downstream ranker, which requires discriminative state representations.

stories.title: Towards Trustworthy Autonomous Robots: An Explainable AI-Based Decision Framework
stories.author: Cagri Temel
bullet_points: Addresses the critical auditability challenge in deep learning-powered autonomous robots.
Introduces TRACE, an Explainable AI (XAI) decision framework to trace robot actions back to sensor evidence.
The framework structures decision-making across four auditable layers, starting with Semantic Perception.

stories.title: Large Language Models (LLMs) for Telecom Root Cause Analysis (RCA): A Structured Reasoning Framework for Evidence-Grounded Diagnosis
stories.author: Zhang
bullet_points: The paper addresses the challenge of performing Root Cause Analysis (RCA) in complex 5G/6G telecom networks.
It proposes a structured reasoning framework to leverage Large Language Models (LLMs) for telecom RCA.
The research aims to mitigate common LLM issues like hallucination and unstable reasoning when dealing with structured network evidence.

stories.title: Dutch Books for Language Models
stories.author: Suproteem Sarkar
bullet_points: The research investigates the reliability of probabilistic forecasts generated by large language models (LLMs).
It addresses the growing user tendency to rely on LLMs for high-stakes life decisions (e.g., economic or disaster risk).
The evaluation method builds upon de Finetti's theorem to assess the coherence of the models' world views.

stories.title: SafeEvolve: Harness-Policy Co-Evolution from Agent Experience for Safety Alignment
stories.author: Dongrui Liu
bullet_points: Introduces SafeEvolve, a novel framework for safety alignment in LLM-based agents.
Addresses safety risks arising from both harmful final outputs and multi-step execution trajectories.
Proposes a co-evolution approach that jointly shapes the base model and the interaction harness using agent experience.

stories.title: Measurement-Driven Sub-Network Selection for On-Premise Retrieval-Augmented Factory Agents
stories.author: Athanasios Bachoumis
bullet_points: Addresses the challenge of deploying large language models (LLMs) for on-premise factory assistants due to hardware constraints.
Proposes a novel approach where model selection is treated as a post-adaptation problem, rather than relying solely on model size.
Demonstrates that retrieval-augmented answer quality is decoupled from general model capability when using structural compression and retrieval-grounded adaptation.

stories.title: A Common Measure of Communication for Speech Brain-Computer Interfaces
stories.author: Oiwi Parker Jones
bullet_points: The research addresses a critical gap in Speech Brain-Computer Interfaces (BCIs): the lack of a standardized metric for measuring progress.
Speech BCIs are a promising technology for restoring speech capabilities in individuals with paralysis.
The current lack of common measures hinders the comparability of research across different BCI systems, datasets, and vocabularies.

stories.title: Discriminative World Models for Web Agents
stories.author: Roei Herzig
bullet_points: The paper addresses a misalignment in current web agent world models, which are trained for next-state prediction (e.g., HTML snapshots).
Existing world models generate fixed representations that are not discriminative enough for downstream ranker models to function effectively.
The research proposes 'Discriminative World Models' to better align the world model's training objective with the needs of the action selection ranker.

stories.title: Graph Machine: Towards Better Pretraining via Edges
stories.author: Lintai Hou
bullet_points: Introduces Graph Machine (GM), a novel architecture designed to improve pretraining efficiency.
GM maintains an $O(n)$-sized state accessible via sparse, dynamic routing, overcoming limitations of fixed-size or static routing methods.
The architecture utilizes differentiable 'edges' (pointer-like objects) for state access, replacing a significant portion of dense Transformer layers.

stories.title: GRADSOLVE: fast exact gradients for ODE ensembles on GPUs
stories.author: Alessio Spurio Mancini
bullet_points: The research addresses a critical bottleneck in scientific computing: obtaining fast, exact gradients for Ordinary Differential Equation (ODE) ensembles on GPUs.
Current GPU solvers present a trade-off, where fast ensemble solvers lack efficient reverse-mode differentiation, and differentiable solvers are too slow.
The proposed method, GRADSOLVE, aims to bridge this gap by providing fast exact gradients for ODE ensembles suitable for GPU acceleration.

stories.title: Improved Gradient Descent Lower Bounds Beyond Nesterov
stories.author: Kaizhao Liu
bullet_points: The research improves theoretical lower bounds for accelerating Gradient Descent (GD) in smooth convex optimization.
It establishes a new non-anytime lower bound of $\Omega(n^{-1.6342})$ and an anytime lower bound of $\Omega(n^{-1.2408})$.
These results surpass previous state-of-the-art lower bounds established by Ma and Chen and Tsai et al.

stories.title: The Implications of Linguistic Illegibility for LLM Security
stories.author: James Mickens
bullet_points: Introduces the concept of 'linguistic illegibility' in Large Language Models (LLMs).
Argues that external linguistic outputs and extracted features may not accurately reflect internal model computation.
Highlights a fundamental challenge in interpreting and understanding how LLMs actually 'think'.

stories.title: Post-Training Language Models for Gold-Medal Performance in Coding Competitions
stories.author: Boris Ginsburg
bullet_points: The research focuses on enhancing Large Language Models (LLMs) for competitive programming, a rigorous test of AI reasoning.
A specialized pipeline combining problem curation, synthetic traces, Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT), and Reinforcement Learning (RL) was developed.
The models trained, Nemotron-3-Nano-CC and Nemotron-3-Ultra-CC, were benchmarked against challenging international coding competitions.

stories.title: UE5M3 FP4 Block Scaling for Stable Language Model Pretraining
stories.author: Paul Balanca
bullet_points: The paper addresses the instability of 4-bit floating-point (FP4) pretraining in language models due to limited magnitude range.
The proposed solution involves pairing E2M1 payloads with unsigned E5M3 block scales to achieve a wider dynamic range.
This method allows for periodic tensor scaling, offering an alternative to existing techniques like NVIDIA's current-tensor scaling.

stories.title: User Feedback Provides a Unique Signal that LLMs Can not Detect
stories.author: Omri Abend
bullet_points: The research proposes that naturally occurring user feedback is a highly actionable learning signal for LLMs.
It challenges the prevailing view that user feedback is inherently too noisy or difficult to leverage effectively.
The study suggests that current evaluation paradigms introduce a systematic bias that masks the true usefulness of user feedback.

stories.title: Post-Training Language Models for Gold-Medal Performance in Coding Competitions
stories.author: Boris Ginsburg
bullet_points: The research focuses on enhancing Large Language Models (LLMs) for competitive programming, a rigorous test of reasoning.
A specialized pipeline combining problem curation, synthetic traces, Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT), and Reinforcement Learning (RL) is introduced.
The models trained, Nemotron-3-Nano-CC and Nemotron-3-Ultra-CC, demonstrate performance improvements in coding competitions.

stories.title: Dutch Books for Language Models
stories.author: Suproteem Sarkar
bullet_points: The paper investigates the coherence of probabilistic forecasts generated by large language models (LLMs).
It addresses the growing user reliance on LLMs for high-stakes life decisions, which often require probabilistic predictions.
The evaluation method builds upon de Finetti's theorem to test the underlying 'world model' consistency of the models.

stories.title: DiscoSign: Discourse-Aware Text to Sign Language Gloss Translation
stories.author: Colin Lea
bullet_points: Introduces DiscoSign, a new computational approach for text-to-sign language gloss translation.
Addresses limitations of traditional sentence-level sign language processing by incorporating discourse-aware features.
Utilizes a modular Large Language Model (LLM) framework to handle complex linguistic phenomena like spatial coreference resolution.

stories.title: EarlyEval: Cheaper Agent Evaluation via Early Outcome Prediction
stories.author: Xiaodong Gu
bullet_points: Addresses the high computational cost of evaluating Large Language Model (LLM) agents.
Introduces 'EarlyEval' and 'early outcome prediction' as a method to reduce evaluation expenses.
Offers a complementary approach to existing benchmark distillation techniques.

stories.title: ShallowStream: Index Shallow then Answer Deep for Streaming Video Understanding
stories.author: Jun Yu
bullet_points: Addresses the computational expense of using Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) for continuous video stream processing.
Proposes 'ShallowStream,' a method designed to efficiently index shallow features before performing deep analysis for streaming video understanding.
Highlights the critical real-world applications of this technology, such as autonomous driving, surveillance, and embodied intelligence.

stories.title: HyperStyler: Low-resource Authorship Style Transfer via Context-aware Style Navigation and Hypernetworks
stories.author: Chiehyeon Lim
bullet_points: The paper introduces HyperStyler, a method for Low-resource Authorship Style Transfer (LAST).
It addresses limitations in existing methods where static author embeddings fail to capture context-dependent stylistic variation.
HyperStyler utilizes Context-aware Style Navigation and Hypernetworks to improve style fidelity while preserving semantic meaning with few examples.

stories.title: False Completion Is the Real Failure Mode of Coding Agents
stories.author: giladha
bullet_points: The article addresses 'false completion,' a critical failure mode in autonomous coding agents.
It proposes a deliberately strict process to mitigate the risk of agents prematurely concluding tasks.
The topic is highly relevant to the current development and reliability challenges in AI software engineering.
